title: Sustainability in daily practice: what the mission asks of you before lunch
vimeoName: Module 10 - Sustainability in daily practice: what the mission asks of you before lunch

segments.text: We've talked about regeneration as a vision.
Now let's bring it down to earth. Literally.
Because sustainability at Craverell isn't a chapter in a report.
It's a hundred small physical actions every day,
done by you. This module is the playbook.
Start with water. We're in the Alentejo.
Water here is not a utility. It's the limiting factor of
everything. The region lives with drought as a neighbor.
That's why the property recycles water. Why the gardens are planned around what
this climate actually gives. Why every drop matters operationally.
For you this means report every leak the hour you see it.
A dripping tap is small. A dripping tap for a month is a scandal.
Housekeeping. Washing routines exist for a reason.
Follow the dosing full loads always. Kitchen.
Sewing under running water is forbidden. Plan ahead instead.
None of this is glamorous. All of it is the mission
in its work clothes. Energy. Same logic.
Air conditioning in an empty house is money and carbon evaporating together.
Check, switch off, close. Lights on walkways and common areas have their
schedules. If you see waste, flag it. The heated indoor pool is one of our
biggest energy commitments. We spend it gladly for guest comfort.
Which is exactly why we don't waste a watt elsewhere.
Waste. And here I want to change how you see it.
At creviro there's no such thing as throwing away.
There is only rooting. Organic scraps root to compost
and compost roots to the farm and the farm roots to the kitchen.
You're not discarding a carrot top. You're sending it on a round trip.
Glass, plastic, paper, oil. Each has its stream and mixing streams out of
laziness breaks the circle we brag about. And before anything becomes
waste at all ask the better question. Why did we
overorder, overproduce, over portion? The cheapest ways to manage is the one that
never happens. Kitchen team. You know this better than anyone.
Full use of the animal, full use of the vegetable,
preservation and fermentation when the garden overwhelms us.
Peek, season, abundance, becoming a winter jam
is the most delicious form of accounting I know.
Purchasing. Every euro we spend is a vote for the world we want.
Local first, seasonal first, real first. When we buy from the honey producer 20
minutes away from the Vicentino vineyards from the
fishermen on this coast. The money stays in the territory
and comes back to us as a stronger more beautiful region
that guests cross Europe to visit. When a supplier decision is yours to
influence, ask the belong questions. Does this strengthen the
territory? Does the value circulate here?
The answer isn't always yes. Sometimes there's no local option
and financial sustainability is a value too.
But the question must always be asked. The farm and the land.
4% built, 96% alive and the 96% needs allies.
Stay on the walkways and paths and help guests do the same.
Gently. If your work touches the land, gardening,
maintenance, the farm itself, you already know
no shortcuts with chemicals, soil is capital, we feed it or we lose it
and guests. Here's the delicate part we never lecture.
Nobody drove from Lisbon to be scolded about towels.
Our way is to make the sustainable choice the beautiful choice.
The organic amenities smell better. The seasonal dish
is the best thing on the menu. The walk to the beach is lovelier than the
drive. When guests ask and they ask more every
year, especially our international guests,
answer with pride and specifics. The 4%, the 70% from the farm,
the compost circle, the laundry that serves the village.
Specifics, not slogans. The difference between greenwashing and the real
thing is that the real thing has numbers and mud
on its boots. Why am I dis insistent? Because coherence is our old brand.
The moment a guest catches a gap between what we preach and what we do,
the regeneration speech next to an overflowing mixed bin.
We're not a farm hotel anymore. We're a marketing exercise with chickens.
I refuse and I can only refuse with your hands because I'm not the one holding
the hose, the thermostat or the purchase order.
You are. Sustainability at Graviral is the sum
of who noticed, who bothered, who did it properly
when nobody was checking. One test and it's yours to keep.
At the end of any shift, ask. Did the place
end my shift a little better or a little worse?
Because I was here. Regeneration is just that question
asked by enough people, answered honestly every single day.
Next module, how we speak. The words we use with guests
and with each other and why they matter more than you think.
